ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a schematic map of regional terrain, transportation, and pipelines. The map on the left marks the 80° and 85° meridians and the 45° latitude line. There are multiple contour lines in the figure; in the southern and southwestern parts the contour lines are relatively dense and the elevation values are relatively high, indicating mountains; the mountains transition northward and northeastward to lower piedmont and plain areas. The legend shows cities, contour lines, oil pipelines, and national highways. The question stem focuses on the appearance of grassland vegetation in the piedmont area in the figure. Then reason: This region belongs to the arid and semi-arid inland background of Central Asia. If it were controlled only by the hydrothermal conditions in the macroscopic latitudinal or longitudinal direction, the natural zones should show a relatively regular zonal distribution. The appearance of grassland at the piedmont is usually related to local water conditions such as precipitation brought by mountain uplift, snow and ice meltwater, and groundwater recharge. It is a difference in natural zone distribution caused by changes in the local environment, and is not continuously developed according to latitudinal zonality or longitudinal zonality. Therefore, what it reflects is the non-zonal phenomenon of natural zones.
